text:
alex: Heads up — canary #2/5 for chart redwood-api v1.4.2 is showing a transient spike in 5xxs (~5%) right after image pull and cache-warmup. Deploy bot marked canary as SUCCESS but telemetry shows error bump at 10:12 UTC. Thinking: fractional rollout pause + manual pin to v1.4.2 for the window.

jamie: When did the image push happen? any registry replication errors?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy completed: chart=redwood-api, release=redwood-api-prod, canary=2/5, image=ghcr.io/redwood/repo:2026-03-19-17, status=SUCCESS, checks=[liveness,readiness,smoke], metrics-url=https://observability/redwood-api/canary/2

priya: I checked registry logs — push succeeded at 09:58 UTC and image sync to eu-west finished by 10:04. No registry 5xxs.

maria: Observability shows a spike in connection pool exhaustion from the cache layer during first minute after pod start. Likely cache warmup causing downstream latency which trips our retry logic -> 503s.

alex: cool, so not an image corruption. Proposal: pause the rollout, pin remaining replicas to previous stable chart (v1.4.1) for the rest of the change window, and run a cache-warmup backfill. We'll also add an explicit prestop hook to drain cache clients more gracefully in the next chart.

kevin: I'm +1 for pause + pin. If we pin, how do we do it safely without cluster churn?

priya: Command to pin the Helm release by forcing the chart version and skipping canary:
```
helm upgrade redwood-api stable/redwood-api --version 1.4.1 --reuse-values --namespace prod --set image.tag=2026-03-15-09 --timeout 10m
kubectl annotate rollout redwood-api rollouts.k8s.io/paused=true -n prod
```

jamie: If we reuse values, ensure we explicitly set the cache init config to the older warmup behavior (oldWarmup.enabled=true). Otherwise the new pod template could still trigger heavy warmups.

maria: I'll kick off a backfill job to pre-warm caching nodes in eu-west. ETA ~15m. Job: `job/cache-warmup --region=eu-west --target=redwood-api-prod`

alex: @deploy-bot please hold auto-promote for this release until manual unpin. Add a note to release notes about warmup regression and hotfix plan.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: auto-promote disabled for release id=rid-20260319-17 by alex. Action logged.

sre-bot: sre-bot: alert suppression applied for canary metric spike for 1 hour to avoid noise while we stabilize.

kevin: If metrics clear after warmup backfill, do we want to continue gradual rollout with a smaller step size (1->2->3) and extended probe timeout?

priya: Yes — smaller increments and extend readiness probe timeout by 10s for warmup window. I'll prepare a candidate values patch: `values.patch` with `canary.stepSize: 1` and `readiness.initialDelaySeconds: 30`.

alex: Plan summary: 1) pause rollout, annotate paused, pin to v1.4.1 2) run cache warmup backfill (maria) 3) adjust canary step size + probe timeout (priya) 4) manual unpin and resume only if 0% 5xx for 10m after warmup. I'll draft the release note blurb and add to the changelog.

jamie: thanks — ping me when warmup job done and I'll run a smoke test against canary #2. :eyes: 

maria: backfill started at 10:22 UTC. will report when complete.

alex: thanks team. updating release notes and ops doc now.

maria: backfill complete at 10:36 UTC. early signals look good, error rate back to baseline.

kevin: smoke test passed at 10:45. ready to unpin if no regressions in next 10m.

alex: unpin plan executed: run helm upgrade to desired chart + set canary.stepSize=1, readiness.initialDelaySeconds=30, then monitor 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: manual promote executed by alex, release=rid-20260319-17, new chart=1.4.2, canary steps=[1,2,5], monitor-window=10m.

sre-bot: sre-bot: monitoring ORB: all clear so far, no spike in 5xx for 8m.

alex: OK resuming. leaving a note in release notes: "Mitigation: paused rollout to pin to 1.4.1 while cache warmup regressed; performed cache warmup and resumed with reduced canary batch size and increased readiness timeout."
